indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a wedding is a union, and a bride is one of its two members
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A trade unionist walks around with a decent wrench in their toolbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union member' and 'spanner' both look like the world of work and tools; the union is a marriage and the spanner is something that spans a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge spans a river or road, so it is literally a thing that spans, which the setter calls a spanner.

parts.note: bum is British slang for the backside
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A rear-end shunt happening in a car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' reads as 'from the rear' in the traffic picture but is a noun for the bottom. In a down clue 'upon' puts the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor knock between two vehicles or objects is commonly called a bump, an everyday synonym for an impact.

clue.text: Gain in material for building over river

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one thing laid over another covers it on both sides, so the outer piece wraps around the inner

parts.note: cement is a basic construction material
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone notes an increase in construction supplies heading over a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition linking 'Gain' to the material, but it is simply the first two letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is a step increase in amount or value, so it is a synonym for an addition or rise.

clue.text: Keep talking about Nintendo console for a child

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to go on is to keep talking at length
the Nintendo DS is a handheld games console

explanation.surface: A parent drones on about which Nintendo machine to buy their kid.
explanation.walkthrough: The present-for-a-child picture hides that 'Keep talking' is a two-word phrase split open to take the console's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A godson is a boy sponsored at baptism by a godparent, so he is a child in that spiritual relationship.

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: faff is British slang for fuss or bother

indicators.note: something in poor shape is out of order, so these letters are badly arranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic grumbles about the bother of sitting through one more dreadful opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Faff, British for pointless fuss, splits after its first letter to take the shuffled letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff is Verdi's final opera, based on Shakespeare's comic knight, so it is a specific example of the art form.

clue.text: Author wants this chair carved in stone

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: agate is a banded semi-precious stone

indicators.note: carving reshapes material into a new form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer commissions a seat sculpted out of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carved in stone' reads as a fixed phrase, but 'carved' rearranges the two words before it and 'in stone' places them inside a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was the English novelist behind Poirot and Miss Marple, a leading writer of detective fiction.

clue.text: Seaweed turned into moss — a grass

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the letters read backwards
the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: a run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: Seaweed has changed into moss and grass, as if in a botany experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant words make the transformation sound literal; read the letters of 'moss a grass' backwards from the end of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargasso is a brown floating seaweed, the gulfweed that gives the Sargasso Sea its name, a type of marine alga.

indicators.note: with its head off a word loses its first letter

parts.note: a thief or fish that is taken has been caught

explanation.surface: A robbery report: nothing stolen, and the culprit has headed off.
explanation.walkthrough: Aught can mean anything, but it is also a variant of ought, the old word for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Aught is an old-fashioned variant of ought, meaning the figure zero, so it serves as a synonym for nil.

clue.text: Clement holds girl in converted van

indicators.note: to hold is to grip around, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: clement weather is mild and fine

indicators.note: something converted has been changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Clement has a girlfriend in a camper van conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement looks like a man's name but is the adjective for mild weather. Van is short for vanguard, the leading part of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard is the foremost position of troops facing an enemy, which is exactly where the front rank exchanging fire stands.

parts.note: surface reading: famous lines taken from Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy
setter's reading: the quotes are the punctuation marks printed around the play's title in the clue itself

explanation.surface: A collection of famous lines lifted from Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Quotes means quotation marks, not quotations; look at the typography of the clue rather than the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks are called by this British name, and they are the marks that enclose a quoted title or speech.

clue.text: Country club refusal to open rally round back

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters read in reverse
to open something is to break into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to rally round someone is to help or support them
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A country club refuses to let a rally start until supporters come back round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' is a false compound: the country is the definition and the club stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia, now officially North Macedonia, is a landlocked Balkan nation, so it is a specific example of a state.

clue.text: Got it right about work returning

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re means concerning or about
to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Someone gets the answer correct about a job coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got it right' looks like the whole definition, but the definition stops at 'Got it' and 'right' gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure this word means message received and understood, so it is used to say understood.

clue.text: Really want those nearest to move ahead

indicators.note: letters made to move change places, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to go on is to go ahead or forward

explanation.surface: Desperate to get ahead of the people closest in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two words 'those nearest' are fodder; 'to move' rearranges them, and the final word supplies the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To set your heart on something is an idiom for longing for it intensely and being determined to have it.

clue.text: Victor, in grief, buys new game

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
something made new is remade, so the letters are given a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grieving man named Victor consoles himself by buying a new game.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor looks like a mourner but is the radio code word for one letter; everything up to 'new' is fodder. Rugby fives is a British handball game played in a walled court, named after Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby fives is a court sport in which players strike a ball with gloved hands, so it is an example of a game.

parts.note: US is short for the United States, so American
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A veteran reporter from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one person, but 'Old' is the definition and the other two words build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Used goods are second-hand, having belonged to someone before, so the word means not new.

parts.note: a shop that carries a product stocks it
to till the soil is to plough it

explanation.surface: A farmer hauls a plough around, as stiff as a statue.
explanation.walkthrough: Both wordplay words read as farm actions; one is the shopkeeper's sense of keeping goods. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing completely motionless is often compared to a statue, which never moves at all.

parts.note: to iron cloth is to smooth it
to foil or cross someone is to thwart them

explanation.surface: An ornament made from shiny metal foil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smooth foil' reads as kitchen wrapping, but both words are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German military medal awarded for bravery, so it is a decoration in the honours sense.

clue.text: Orchestra member wants wine to drink at home

indicators.note: something drunk is taken inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A musician would like a glass of wine at home after the concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The orchestra member is an instrument, not a player; the wine does the drinking here.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a woodwind instrument with a regular seat in the symphony orchestra, so it is one of its members.

parts.note: to battle is to struggle
the ore is a coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Someone fought with a foreign exchange scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like a swindle with money, but it is the bat used in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is the small bat used in the old game of battledore and shuttlecock, a forerunner of badminton.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sad, low in spirits
second meaning: the soft fine plumage of birds

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a bird's colouring; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means dejected as an adjective, and as a noun the fluffy under-plumage of young birds used in pillows.

clue.text: Not so much work, for example

parts.note: less means a smaller amount
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A reduced workload, to give one case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like a sign-off, but 'example' is the definition, as in a warning to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishment meant as a warning to others is called both an example and a lesson, as in let that be a lesson.

parts.note: surface reading: brightly coloured insects from the rainforest
setter's reading: tropical means relating to a trope, and butterflies for nerves is a non-literal expression

explanation.surface: Exotic butterflies cited as an instance of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A trope is a figurative use of words, so 'tropical' here means figurative; having butterflies in the stomach is such a usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression used non-literally, like butterflies for nervousness, is called a trope in rhetoric.

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Details printed on a pair of bottles of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled spirits' reads as liquor, but these spirits live in bottles and lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a genie is a magic being trapped in a lamp or bottle, and this is a plural form of that word.

clue.text: Wife slices chicken to be carved

indicators.note: a blade that slices goes into something, so one piece cuts inside the other

parts.note: a hen is a female chicken
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife carves up the roast chicken for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slices' looks like the carving itself, but it signals the letter cutting into the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn is the past participle of hew, to chop or shape with a blade, so it matches carved.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a vein carries blood back to the heart
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A newly discovered toxin found in the bloodstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In blood vessel' reads as where the toxin is, but 'In' is the container signal for the new letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Venin is a technical term for the toxic substance in snake venom, so it is a kind of toxin.

parts.note: misses are young unmarried women, or maids
the tone of a meeting is its spirit or mood

explanation.surface: A prisoner pines for freedom and lost morale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misses' reads as a verb of longing but is a plural noun. HMP Maidstone is a prison in the county town of Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: HM Prison Maidstone is a well-known British jail, so the town's name stands for that institution.

definitions.note: a joke superlative of skint, British slang for having no money
definitions.meaning: first meaning: most broke, the superlative of British slang for penniless
second meaning: a medical check where substances are applied to the arm

explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money; add the superlative ending and the run of letters splits differently into the medical phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Allergists apply small amounts of allergens to the skin and watch for a reaction, which is the standard diagnostic check.

clue.text: Cancun is only holding this concert

indicators.note: words holding something keep it inside them, so the letters sit within the text

parts.note: a run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: The Mexican resort of Cancun is putting on just this one concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' reads as a show, but it means agreement, as in acting in concert.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert or in unison is to act together in agreement, so the two nouns are synonyms.
